title: When the Echo Wakes Again
premise: Hazel Galloway, a xenolinguist exiled to the forgotten colony of Vesper's Rest after a translation error she believes caused a massacre, records the colony's quiet collapse while losing her ability to dream in human languages. When a distress signal arrives in Ashkari—a language extinct for two hundred years—she realizes the colony sits atop the buried archive of the Ashkar, a species the war's victors erased, and that the signal carries a message that could end the war by exposing the victors' founding crime. Hunted by both the Republic and the insurgent Concord, Hazel must choose between translating the truth and protecting the colonists she has come to love. She broadcasts the archive, ending the war but shattering the Republic, and in the aftermath finally dreams again—in Ashkari.
about_author: Ivo Reyes is the pen name of a former field linguist who spent a decade documenting dying languages before turning to science fiction. Their work explores how memory survives in speech, and what it costs to be the last one listening.

chapters.title: The Quiet Census
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. On Vesper's Rest, Hazel records the colony's dwindling population for an archive no one reads, noting the water rationing and the silence in her dreams. She interviews old Marek, the last fluent speaker of a settler dialect. Emotional beat: melancholy routine, the ache of being a witness no one wants.

chapters.title: Dreams Without Words
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. She wakes from a dream structured in no human grammar, terrified and exhilarated. Her colleague Devi notices her sleep-talking in an unknown cadence. Flashback hints at the translation error that ended her career. Emotional beat: creeping self-estrangement, the fear that she is becoming something else.

chapters.title: Signal in a Dead Tongue
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. The colony's derelict relay array, which Hazel maintains out of stubbornness, catches a burst transmission. Her analysis software fails; the phonology matches Ashkari, a language exterminated with its speakers two centuries ago. Emotional beat: electric shock of the impossible, guilt stirring like sediment.

chapters.title: What the Republic Forgot to Burn
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV, with an interlude of Republic archivist Sennet's memos. Hazel deciphers fragments suggesting the Ashkar archive lies beneath the colony itself—the colony was built as a cap over the evidence. Emotional beat: dawning horror that her exile was engineered.

chapters.title: Devi's Bargain
chapters.summary: Devi's POV. Devi, secretly reporting to the Republic, wrestles with her orders to confirm and then erase the signal. She loves Hazel and the colony. Emotional beat: complicity and tenderness at war; the reader learns the surveillance net before Hazel does.

chapters.title: The Grammar of Grief
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Deciphering Ashkari, Hazel discovers the language encodes grief grammatically—every past-tense verb marks who was lost. Her dreams shift fully into Ashkari. Emotional beat: intimacy with the dead, the vertigo of learning to feel in a murdered tongue.

chapters.title: Concord at the Gate
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. An insurgent Concord ship arrives seeking the signal, offering the starving colony supplies in exchange for the archive. Captain Oyelaran is pragmatic, not monstrous. Emotional beat: seduction of rescue with strings attached; Hazel sees her chance and her cage.

chapters.title: Rations and Ruin
chapters.summary: Marek's POV. The colony fractures: some want to trade Hazel's discovery for food, others fear the Republic's reprisal. A ration riot kills two. Emotional beat: survival grinding community down; the theme of power's corruption at human scale.

chapters.title: The Error That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Devi, cracking under guilt, reveals the truth: Hazel's 'translation error' was a Republic false flag—the massacre was deliberate, and Hazel was scapegoated to bury the Ashkar connection. Emotional beat: rage and terrible relief; her shame was someone's weapon.

chapters.title: Sennet Descends
chapters.summary: Sennet's POV. The Republic archivist lands with a 'relief mission' and a quiet mandate: erase the archive, the signal, and anyone who touched them. Sennet is courteous, thorough, and utterly corrupt. Emotional beat: cold dread; evil as paperwork.

chapters.title: Under the Colony
chapters.summary: Hazel, Devi, and Oyelaran's POV alternating. They breach the buried archive: a living repository of Ashkar minds, half-awake, broadcasting for two centuries to no one. Emotional beat: awe and grief; the dead were never finished speaking.

chapters.title: The Message
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. The archive's message is not a plea but testimony—a full record of the Republic's extermination, addressed to both sides of the war. Delivering it could end the war or ignite total conflict. Emotional beat: the weight of a choice that belongs to everyone.

chapters.title: Sides
chapters.summary: Devi's POV. Devi must choose: warn Sennet to protect her family in Republic space, or stand with Hazel. She burns her reports. Emotional beat: betrayal inverted into sacrifice; love as defection.

chapters.title: The Siege of Small Things
chapters.summary: Marek's POV. Republic forces blockade the colony; Concord ships hold orbit; civilians starve between them. Marek organizes a quiet resistance of farmers and teachers. Emotional beat: stubborn dignity, the price of survival paid in ordinary lives.

chapters.title: Interrogation of a Witness
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Sennet takes Hazel aboard his ship, offering her reinstatement and absolution if she declares the signal a forgery. He shows her the massacre records—her name in the falsified report. Emotional beat: temptation of erasure; power corrupting through kindness.

chapters.title: What Hazel Dreams
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Imprisoned, Hazel dreams fully in Ashkari and wakes understanding the message completely—and what it will cost: the archive's broadcast will burn out the repository, killing the last Ashkar minds. Emotional beat: the cruelest price; truth demands the death of the tellers.

chapters.title: The Escape That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Oyelaran and Devi's POV. The Concord raid to free Hazel goes wrong; Devi is captured covering Hazel's escape. Oyelaran reveals Concord plans to weaponize the archive, not free it. Emotional beat: allies revealed as buyers; Hazel has no clean hands to shake.

chapters.title: Every Ear in the System
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Hazel returns to the archive and begins the translation-broadcast, using the colony's relay array and her own Ashkari-fluent mind as the bridge. Sennet's forces breach the surface. Emotional beat: desperate momentum; a race between testimony and erasure.

chapters.title: The Broadcast
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converging. As Republic troops storm the archive, Hazel completes the transmission: the Ashkar testimony floods every channel in the system. The archive's minds begin to fade. Emotional beat: climax—catharsis and loss entwined; the dead speak at last, and then are gone.

chapters.title: Aftermath of a Sentence
chapters.summary: Devi's and Sennet's POVs. The Republic fractures; Sennet, his crime now public record, chooses quiet self-erasure. Devi is freed in the chaos. The war stalls as soldiers on both sides read the same testimony. Emotional beat: the strange anticlimax of truth—no victory parade, only reckoning.

chapters.title: The Colony That Remained
chapters.summary: Marek's and Hazel's POVs. Vesper's Rest, revealed as the war's moral center, receives aid and pilgrims. Hazel buries the archive's final carrier, honoring the Ashkar's choice to spend themselves on truth. Emotional beat: grief with ground under it; the price paid, counted honestly.

chapters.title: When the Echo Wakes Again
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV, coda. Months later, Hazel teaches colony children Ashkari words from memory, keeping a language alive that no longer has native speakers. She dreams, and for the first time the dream is hers—Ashkari and human braided together. Emotional beat: quiet renewal; identity rebuilt from what survived.
